text:
alex: Quick follow-up on FA v2/v3 perf deltas after yesterday's RFC merge. Seeing a 6-12% p99 tail increase on v3 for short seqs on A100s. Anyone else?

maria: Yup, caught that in staging around 10:30. Short seqs (<=64), small batches (1-4). Throughput unchanged.

raj: Could be workspace fragmentation with the tiled kernels in v3. v2's single-shot kernel handled tiny buffers better.

jen: Ran a quick diff. When we disable block-splitting padding for short inputs, v3 latency drops to v2 levels. Patch: `runtime.allocator.pad_short_seqs=false`

jen: Perf snippet:
```
model: llama-13b
hw: a100-40gb
seq 32, batch 2
v2 p99 48ms
v3 p99 54ms (pad disabled -> 49ms)
```

ci-bot: Benchmark job #432 finished: artifacts at https://ci/internal/bench/432 :green_heart:

alex: Interesting — so padding/fragmentation heuristics matter. Short-term idea: automatic fallthrough to v2 for seq<=64 or when allocator fragmentation high. Thoughts?

maria: SGTM as a quick mitigation. We need a per-model flag so hosted users can opt-in/out and we can A/B. Also add telemetry to see how often fallback triggers.

raj: We should emit kernel-contract telemetry: requested workspace, allocated fragments, pad bytes, kernel variant chosen. That will let us tune the heuristic instead of a blunt seq cutoff.

jen: I'll draft a follow-up RFC with experiments, rollout plan, and telemetry schema. Plan: 1) enable telemetry, 2) canary fallback to v2 for 24h on dedicated pool, 3) measure impact on cost/latency.

alex: Sounds good. @ops can we spin up a dedicated canary with v3 enabled + fallback policy? Need ~100 GPUs for 2h window to get stables stats.

ops: We can provision a canary pool. PR to infra with tag `fa3-canary-1961` and we'll schedule for tomorrow 02:00 UTC.

maria: Also flag to watch: quantized bf16 path had small regressed tails in one vendor driver — include driver version in telemetry.

raj: Agree. Also add a slow-path counter so we can see how often kernel falls back to a slower kernel within v3.

jen: Opening RFC now: https://go/repo/rfcs/flashattn-v3-fallbacks-1961

alex: Thanks all. If anyone sees other oddness (memory spikes, OOMs) drop them here. We'll keep this thread as the tracker until the RFC lands. :mag:
